shoal_e18_entry.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_entry.text: On Day Three Hundred Sixty-Six, Song Mei arrived at the public performance room before its ordinary musicians. She was carrying a plain travel case Yue had never seen. It held costumes and permitted copies for a tour she had negotiated herself. The port's recent work had not suspended her artistic contracts. She would leave on a booked southern route after the current performances, well before Yue's possible journey toward the mine.

shoal_e18_open_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_open_02.text: Yue helped open an ordinary door while Song brought the case through. Song placed it clear of the exit and said the venue keeper would receive it later under the accepted short custody. A new piece needed rehearsal. She had changed its ending again, which pleased her and annoyed the musician who had just learned the previous version. His irritation did not mean he wanted her to stop writing.

shoal_e18_open_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_open_03.text: They greeted each other, then began arguing about where the singer could actually take a breath. Song wanted the final accusation to arrive before the audience felt comfortable. The musician wanted a human throat left to deliver it. Yue sat where the keeper permitted ordinary observers and heard them try a slower opening. Neither artist was pretending a cultivation method could replace the work of rehearsing the actual song.

shoal_e18_open_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_open_04.text: Before the rehearsal, Song asked what had become of the earlier offered audience work. The sheets and private oral reprise had made different people hear different things. Their actual current access would shape the invitation she was prepared to offer now. She would not act as though a printed sale had been a private testimony, or a private story had granted a public performance license. Yue named the work she had actually fulfilled.

shoal_e18_art_gate.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_art_gate.text: Song opened the earlier performance note and checked the actual offered scope before making a new invitation. An ordinary sale could leave public readers; a consenting oral reprise could leave private listeners. Neither choice had purchased her next song or her future road. The present invitation would grow from what those people had actually received and what they were now willing to offer.

shoal_e18_sheets_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_sheets_01.text: Eight printed sheets had actually sold during the offered interval. Their buyers held the ordinary household-reading rights stated on that edition. Song had received ten copper from the performance and sales after paying Yue's completed two-copper assistant task, not an imaginary sum from the private reprise she had declined. Those copies had remained in actual households while the harbor worked through its fire and account disputes.

shoal_e18_sheets_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_sheets_02.text: A teacher who bought one asked Song for a new bounded school reading. Purchasing the sheet had not granted a public adaptation or an exclusive hold on the performer. The teacher supplied the current school request, date, audience, and separate twelve-copper art allocation. Song considered its actual terms and accepted one ordinary reading after rehearsal. She would retain her new ending rather than let the school make it more reassuring without her agreement.

shoal_e18_sheets_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_sheets_03.text: Yue was invited as the person who had actually helped the earlier copies reach readers, with no authority over the school program. She could attend its offered public hours. The teacher wanted a permitted current excerpt and would receive only what Song chose to license for that reading. Song's travel case remained hers. Neither the school nor the Six-Reach association could claim its contents because it had paid one art fee.

shoal_e18_sheets_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_sheets_04.text: The reading took place before an ordinary afternoon class. Song introduced the distinction between a poem about a fire and a checked account of a fire. A child asked whether a poem could tell truth without naming every person. She said it could describe a feeling truly and still leave facts unproven. The teacher asked them to name what kind of claim each line was actually making before repeating it as history.

shoal_e18_sheets_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_sheets_05.text: One child wanted the new ending changed so the town won everything back. Song declined. Another wanted every supplier punished. She declined that too. The piece's workers had different choices, and the last line left a loss standing. She sang it once at the ordinary agreed volume, without demanding that the children like it. A public audience had the freedom to be confused, disappointed, or moved by an artist's actual work.

shoal_e18_sheets_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_sheets_06.text: The teacher received the licensed excerpt under its limited school-use terms and paid the accepted twelve copper after the actual reading. Song put it in her own art account, which paid her own working expenses and future road. Yue received no second assistant wage merely for sitting among listeners. The current school performance was new paid work made possible by public readers, not a retroactive increase in the earlier sale.

shoal_e18_sheets_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_sheets_07.text: After the class, a child offered a drawing of the musician as a gull stealing notes. Song asked whether the child meant to give it to her. He did, and she accepted the actual gift. The teacher did not keep it as school property because it had been drawn during the lesson. The musician examined it later and said the beak was accurate. He would not agree that his nose was.

shoal_e18_sheets_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_sheets_08.text: The two people who might have heard the earlier private oral reprise had not heard it then. One had left on an actual work road before this school invitation. Song would not claim the public reading substituted for a private conversation she had never offered him. The sheets had opened a new audience and left another opportunity unfulfilled. Yue could see both without asking Song to fit them into a single happy account.

shoal_e18_sheets_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_sheets_09.text: A school visitor asked to copy the entire new song after seeing the excerpt. Song refused the broader request and explained the license actually offered. The visitor could buy the published edition if Song later chose to publish it. Yue did not hand over a remembered line to rescue the visitor from disappointment. Helping distribute an earlier sheet did not make her a second owner of the performer's unoffered work.

shoal_e18_sheets_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_sheets_10.text: The teacher asked whether Yue wanted to explain the fire response to the class. Yue accepted only the actual ordinary receiving and ordinary-response facts she had witnessed, with the corrected drawing's distinction intact. She did not tell the children she had stood inside flames or powered a wall against the sea. The class was interested in a crew's repeated instructions to move back from a rope, which pleased the musician's sense of rhythm.

shoal_e18_sheets_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_sheets_11.text: Song closed the school reading at its accepted hour. Her current art fee had been paid, the excerpt's scope recorded, and the broader song retained under her own rights. She had made a useful public appearance and still wanted to leave on her independent tour. The school could invite another performance later through its actual process. A successful class did not turn her next season into public property.

shoal_e18_sheets_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_sheets_12.text: Yue carried no school mandate out of the doorway. She had received a different sort of acquaintance with Song: public readers could now ask precise questions about a work they actually held. It was a gain with limits. The private reprise missed earlier stayed missed. Song returned to the rehearsal room because her booked road needed a finished piece and the musician still thought the opening could be improved.

shoal_e18_oral_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_oral_01.text: The two consenting listeners had actually heard the private oral reprise. Its story had not been printed, and Yue had not sold its sentences to fill unsold sheets. Song had retained two copper from the performance after paying Yue's completed assistant task, while the eight sheets remained her unsold stock. The private hour had left a relationship with two actual people rather than a public audience holding new copies.

shoal_e18_oral_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_oral_02.text: One listener still worked near the quay and asked whether Song would hear a current private account before her southern road. The other had departed on an ordinary family journey and sent no new testimony. Song considered the offered visit and accepted one finite conversation. It would be neither a public performance nor a promise to turn the worker's words into a song. Yue was invited only if the speaker wished her there.

shoal_e18_oral_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_oral_03.text: The speaker did wish her there as the person who had helped arrange the earlier private hour. She offered a narrow ordinary account about listening for bells while working under a roof whose noise obscured them. She did not offer clinical details or her household's finances. Song asked questions about sound and ordinary attention. Yue listened without converting the visit into technical qualification for a new warning device.

shoal_e18_oral_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_oral_04.text: The worker described a rhythm by tapping the table. Song tried it, then said the actual bell's pause would matter more than a pretty pattern. They went to the public lane at the next ordinary bell and listened from where pedestrians were permitted. The worker could show what she heard without entering a restricted bench. A private relationship had made an ordinary observation possible that a printed sale had not supplied.

shoal_e18_oral_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_oral_05.text: The sound disappeared beneath a loaded cart's rattle. They waited for the next permitted observation rather than pretending they had heard it clearly. Song asked whether the account could be used in a new piece. The worker declined its private sentences and permitted only a general description of interrupted hearing without her name. Song accepted that narrower scope. An offered story could change what an artist noticed without becoming words she owned.

shoal_e18_oral_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_oral_06.text: No school had bought the earlier eight sheets during Yue's offered sales interval. The teacher who might have made that connection had not received a copy then. A public school invitation did not materialize simply because the private conversation was useful. Song's actual current tour budget remained supported by her other earned art work and savings. She would not manufacture twelve copper of school income from an unperformed reading.

shoal_e18_oral_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_oral_07.text: The worker asked to hear the revised song privately once its rehearsal was ready. Song offered a specific short listening time under the venue keeper's accepted hours, with no new fee and no demand for endorsement. Yue could attend only under the speaker's continuing invitation. The new room would contain actual people who had already trusted one another with a limited story, not an imagined class whose public license had never been offered.

shoal_e18_oral_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_oral_08.text: At the short listening, the worker liked the first passage and disliked the ending. Song asked why. She said she wanted a place to breathe after a week of hearing bad news. Song understood and kept the ending. Her piece intended to leave the listener with an unresolved cost. The worker could dislike that artistic choice without having betrayed the earlier private conversation. She thanked Song for asking and said she would prefer another song tonight.

shoal_e18_oral_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_oral_09.text: The musician played an older permitted tune after Song agreed it fit the remaining offered time. The worker knew it and quietly joined one ordinary refrain. Yue knew only part and listened. Their moment did not solve the warning problem or produce a clinical recovery. It let a person who had offered a difficult account spend a few minutes with something she enjoyed. Song could respect that without changing the new piece.

shoal_e18_oral_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_oral_10.text: Before leaving, the worker confirmed that her private sentences remained unlicensed for copying. Song put the general permitted observation in a separate note and returned the speaker's own written scrap. Yue kept neither. The wider school audience that an actual sheet sale might have created still did not exist here. The gain was a narrower living relationship whose boundaries mattered precisely because the people had chosen to speak.

shoal_e18_oral_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_oral_11.text: Song closed the offered listening time when the venue's next ordinary use began. The worker returned to her own current responsibilities. There was no unearned public fee or applause to balance the missed sheet sales. Yue had helped preserve a private hour, and now she could hear how that hour affected an artist's attention without purchasing the artist's future decisions. Song still had a booked southern road.

shoal_e18_oral_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_oral_12.text: Yue returned with Song to the rehearsal table. The private listener's disagreement had not made the new ending less deliberate. Song wanted the musician to hear where the worker had wished for breath and decide whether the opening made the cost clear. They tried one ordinary change in pace. The song became different through actual rehearsal. The listener's private account remained with its owner, beyond the part she had chosen to permit.

shoal_e18_art_rejoin_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_art_rejoin_01.text: After rehearsal Yue asked whether Song wanted to consider the mine road together if a new scope became available. Song said no before Yue described all its possible uses. She had booked a southern tour and wanted the audiences there. She was not choosing between caring about Yue and caring about strangers. She was choosing her own working season, for which she had negotiated dates, people, and actual payment.

shoal_e18_art_rejoin_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_art_rejoin_02.text: Yue began explaining that a mine might need an independent witness. Song stopped her gently and said a need did not make it her appointment. Other suitable people could be invited under terms they accepted. She wanted to sing the piece she had just finished and visit her sister after the tour's last stop. Yue had known some of those plans and still imagined a road that fit her own new interests first.

shoal_e18_art_rejoin_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_art_rejoin_03.text: The refusal hurt more than Yue expected. She had not meant to claim Song's future and had nevertheless been picturing it beside hers. She said she understood, then admitted she was disappointed. Song said disappointment was an answer she could live with. She did not want an argument proving her already-booked road inferior. The two women could remain close enough to speak honestly without promising the same destination.

shoal_e18_art_rejoin_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_art_rejoin_04.text: Song asked whether Yue wanted advice about traveling with artists. Yue said she probably needed advice about asking any independent person. Song laughed and said a useful invitation included room to refuse without receiving a speech about all the good that might have been done. Yue wrote no lesson in her practice notebook. The exchange belonged to this relationship, and the apology could stay plain.

shoal_e18_art_rejoin_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_art_rejoin_05.text: The musician pretended to examine his fiddle while giving them privacy at the table. Afterward he asked whether the mine had ordinary music worth hearing. He was curious, not accepting a post. Song threatened to make him carry her heaviest costume case if he began planning a second tour before completing this one. He answered that every case became heavier when a singer revised its contents.

shoal_e18_art_rejoin_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_art_rejoin_06.text: Yue offered one actual farewell help interval before Song's departure. Song had two different requests she was willing to accept: an ordinary beginner's lesson in listening and speaking rhythm, or help inventorying the tour case while the musician rehearsed. They overlapped in her available afternoon. One would give Yue a small personal skill; the other would finish useful road work and offer a closer look at how an artist actually prepared to leave.

shoal_e18_art_rejoin_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_art_rejoin_07.text: The lesson was no qi qualification. Song would teach ordinary breath pacing, attention, and a refrain suitable for a beginner's voice. Yue's six pairs would not make her a trained singer. The case inventory was no license to copy unreleased work. It required ordinary receiving skills, labels, and the owner's accepted items. Song offered both without charging a fee because she wanted to spend one particular hour with Yue before the road.

shoal_e18_art_rejoin_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_art_rejoin_08.text: Yue asked whether accepting the inventory would mean she had agreed to accompany the tour. Song said it would mean the case had been inventoried. They laughed at the need for the answer. A gift of useful time did not need to become a secret contract for more. The musician had his own paid work and could complete the rehearsal without Yue, just as Song could pack later if Yue chose the lesson.

shoal_e18_art_rejoin_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_art_rejoin_09.text: On Day Three Hundred Seventy-One, before the offered afternoon, Bo completed his eighth and final four-copper rehabilitation session under the finite deposit. Thirty-two had funded actual sessions; the earlier brace had used eight, completing the forty-copper support line. The current practitioner observed limited staff-assisted walking and kept heavy hauling prohibited. No perfect leg had been promised, and none was declared because the account could now close.

shoal_e18_art_rejoin_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_art_rejoin_10.text: With initial care thirty-two, support forty, actual travel eight, restricted-income thirty, and dressings ten, all one hundred twenty had been spent on performed accepted scopes. Bo retained his brace and current ordinary care instructions. Later needs would require actual new arrangements, including what he and Jin could afford or properly request. The complete account did not make his remaining impairment vanish. It showed what the finite help had actually done.

shoal_e18_art_rejoin_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_art_rejoin_11.text: Yue visited briefly under Bo and Jin's offered terms. He demonstrated no heroic distance for her. He described the narrower work he could now accept and a customer who insisted a repaired stool should look new. Jin said the stool was older than the customer's stated patience. Yue left them laughing and went to Song's offered afternoon with the knowledge that a completed term could leave a real changed life behind it.

shoal_e18_farewell_choice.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_farewell_choice.text: Before her independent southern tour, Song offered Yue one finite afternoon. She could teach an ordinary beginner's rhythm lesson, or accept help inventorying the actual tour case while her musician rehearsed. The lesson gave personal practice; the inventory completed road preparation and permitted only the owner's offered view of her work. Song's destination remained her own. Yue chose the offered hour she wanted to share.

choices.text: Take Song's ordinary beginner's rhythm lesson.
Inventory the tour case under Song's actual permissions.

shoal_e18_lesson_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_lesson_01.text: Song began by asking Yue to speak a plain line without hurrying its last word. Yue obeyed with the seriousness she usually brought to a measured marker task. Song told her the line was not a test intended to catch her cheating. It was a way to hear what her ordinary voice did when she expected judgment. Yue tried again and found herself laughing before she reached the ending.

shoal_e18_lesson_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_lesson_02.text: They practiced a short refrain with no energy routed into the task. Song listened for ordinary tension in the phrasing and stopped when Yue pushed through a breath to appear capable. She offered another place to pause. The change made the refrain easier and less impressive to an imaginary audience. The audience actually present was one teacher who preferred a novice's clear note to a heroic strain she would have to repair later.

shoal_e18_lesson_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_lesson_03.text: Yue asked whether cultivation breathing made the exercise easier. Song said she could hear Yue's voice, not certify a body method. A qualified inner route did not tell her where an ordinary song wanted its phrase. Yue listened to the musician demonstrate the passage and noticed that his quieter version carried the words farther into her attention. It was a different craft, with different evidence of success.

shoal_e18_lesson_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_lesson_04.text: For a moment she wished she had begun learning years earlier. Song said years earlier was unavailable this afternoon. A beginner could do the current small work without apologizing for every year she had spent doing something else. Yue tried the refrain once more at the permitted ordinary pace. She missed a note. Song corrected it and moved on, giving the error exactly as much importance as the next useful attempt required.

shoal_e18_lesson_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_lesson_05.text: They went to the public doorway and listened to the tide bell against a passing cart. Song asked Yue to reproduce only the rhythm she had actually heard. Yue initially filled the interrupted section from expectation. Song waited for another ordinary bell and showed the difference. Listening was work before it became performance. The lesson did not qualify Yue to design a warning signal; it taught her to notice where her own hearing had guessed.

shoal_e18_lesson_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_lesson_06.text: The musician returned from a short errand and asked to hear the refrain. Yue could decline and chose to try it once. He listened without treating a missed note as humiliation. He suggested a lower starting pitch suited to her ordinary voice. Song tried the adjustment and accepted it for this lesson. Their collaboration gave Yue a small usable method rather than a claim she was secretly gifted enough to skip practice.

shoal_e18_lesson_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_lesson_07.text: Meanwhile the tour case remained un-inventoried during that offered interval. Song would complete its receiving check later in her own scheduled preparation. The unchosen help had not occurred somewhere beyond the room. She lost an hour she might have used to finish sooner, and the musician would need to wait for its actual completion before receiving the final case list. Neither demanded Yue repay that cost after accepting the lesson.

shoal_e18_lesson_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_lesson_08.text: At the hour's end, Yue could sing the short refrain once at an ordinary comfortable pace and knew where she still missed a note. Song gave permission to practice that published refrain personally, with no public-performance license implied. Yue thanked her for the actual teaching, not for opening a route inside her body. She had learned something small from a woman whose road she could not own.

shoal_e18_lesson_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_lesson_09.text: Song then closed the lesson and turned to the preparation she still needed to complete. Yue offered no last-minute promise to make up the inventory while also keeping the whole afternoon's other plans. She had accepted one hour and received its particular gain. She left the performer to her current work. Outside, she quietly tried the line once while walking, then stopped because the lane required more attention than the song.

shoal_e18_lesson_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_lesson_10.text: That evening Yue wrote the ordinary refrain's title beside the name of the person who had taught it. She recorded no stage increase and claimed no talent beyond the small practiced passage. The memory gave her a way to carry Song's offered hour into a later lonely road. It did not make Song present on that road or turn her independent departure into a promise to follow after all.

shoal_e18_case_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_case_01.text: Song opened the tour case after identifying which contents she offered for inventory. Yue read the ordinary list aloud while Song checked each accepted item. Two costume layers, a plain outer coat, permitted working copies, and a small repair kit belonged to the performer. The musician's separate instrument and papers were not inside this case. Receiving one owner's property did not grant a view of another person's pack.

shoal_e18_case_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_case_02.text: A revised working copy had the wrong edition label. Yue caught it when Song's spoken description did not match the case list. Song corrected the actual label and destroyed no older manuscript in a fit of artistic certainty. The older version would remain in its proper private storage. The current tour needed the version she intended to perform, which was enough of a problem to deserve an ordinary careful check.

shoal_e18_case_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_case_03.text: The case's side pocket contained a letter to Song's sister. Yue did not read it. She entered one sealed personal letter under the offered inventory terms and asked whether Song wanted it traveling in the case or in her own smaller bag. Song chose the smaller bag because she intended to send it at the first ordinary stop. The decision belonged to the owner who knew the letter's actual purpose.

shoal_e18_case_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_case_04.text: They checked the case latch with permission and found a worn ordinary strap that Song wanted replaced before departure. The venue keeper directed her to a current craftsperson with available hours. She paid from her own received art income after accepting the repair scope. Yue neither routed energy through the latch nor declared it safe on the basis of a cultivation record. The case needed an ordinary strap suited to its actual road use.

shoal_e18_case_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_case_05.text: The musician rehearsed while they worked. He had accepted his own paid part of the tour and wanted Song to hear a changed passage before the evening ended. She listened after completing the item list, leaving the case shut but not yet received for travel. A rehearsal could continue beside road preparation without one pretending to complete the other. Yue heard how a faster phrase made Song's new ending harder to speak clearly.

shoal_e18_case_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_case_06.text: Song tried the passage and rejected the musician's change after a genuine attempt. He argued, then tried the earlier version with one smaller adjustment. Yue offered no artistic ruling because she had been useful with labels. The performers resolved their own work. Her access let her see more of their preparation, not become the person whose opinion settled every disagreement in the room.

shoal_e18_case_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_case_07.text: The repaired strap returned through the craftsperson's actual receiving before the venue closed. Song inspected the performed repair under its ordinary terms and accepted it. The case then passed its owner's current packing check with its offered contents listed correctly. Yue supplied the clean copy for the named carrier receiving. The tour preparation had advanced by a real hour's work and a specific caught error.

shoal_e18_case_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_case_08.text: No beginner's lesson had occurred during that interval. Yue had listened to a rehearsal, which was not the same as being taught an ordinary refrain with feedback. She could ask for a future lesson only if Song later offered one through actual time and terms. The missed personal opportunity remained missed. Useful clerical work had gained her a closer view of the performer's departure, and that gain had its own shape.

shoal_e18_case_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_case_09.text: Song thanked Yue for catching the edition mismatch. The thanks concerned the work performed, not an endorsement of every later request Yue might make. She retained the private versions, the sealed letter, and all rights not offered for the tour. Yue returned the temporary working list after its accepted copy had been made. An orderly inventory could help an independent person leave rather than become another reason to keep her in town.

shoal_e18_case_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_case_10.text: That evening Yue remembered the case's unremarkable contents more vividly than its imagined stage glamour. Artists traveled with repair kits, clean cloth, sealed letters, and work still subject to disagreement. The memory made Song's independent road easier to understand and no easier to share. Yue had chosen to help it become ready. She would carry that particular farewell instead of a song lesson she had not taken.

shoal_e18_close_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_close_01.text: On Day Three Hundred Seventy-Two, Song completed the preparation still due under her own tour plan and received the carrier's actual final list. The items traveling belonged to their named owners and held their respective permissions. Yue was not listed as a passenger. The fact stood plainly enough to hurt without becoming an accusation. Song had accepted useful time from her and was now leaving on the road she had chosen.

shoal_e18_close_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_close_02.text: The last harbor performance used Song's revised ending. Some listeners applauded immediately; others remained quiet until the musician lowered his fiddle. A supplier disliked the piece and left before the final refrain. Song did not demand his approval. The ordinary ticket account paid its accepted venue and musician scopes before leaving her actual share. Yue attended under her own paid ticket and claimed no special seat through their friendship.

shoal_e18_close_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_close_03.text: Afterward a listener told Song the ending was cruel because it left the workers with something still lost. Song asked whether the listener meant the actual loss or hearing it sung. He answered slowly, then said both. She accepted the complaint as his response to the piece. She would consider it in future writing if she wished. She would not change this already-performed ending while the room waited for everyone to agree.

shoal_e18_close_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_close_04.text: Yue helped carry only her own small bag from the room. The venue keeper and actual carrier handled the performers' property under their accepted roles. Song came outside without making a public farewell speech about the port's recovery. She wanted a hot meal and enough sleep for the morning. The musician wanted to hear whether she intended to revise the ending on the coach. She said probably, which made him groan.

shoal_e18_close_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_close_05.text: They ate at a place Song chose and each paid the actual agreed share from personal received money. Yue stayed within the small spending she had planned. The meal had fish, greens, and bread better than the inn's usual loaf. Song told a story about a stage curtain that fell at precisely the worst line of a solemn song. The audience had laughed and the performers had survived its laughter by finishing the work.

shoal_e18_close_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_close_06.text: Yue asked whether Song remembered the first time an audience refused her intended feeling. Song said most audiences refused part of it. A performance was an offered work, not an instrument for controlling everyone in a room. Yue recognized the temptation to want a choice of hers understood exactly as she intended. Song said understanding was often partial even between people who liked each other. They ordered more ordinary hot water and let the thought rest.

shoal_e18_close_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_close_07.text: The musician left first because he had an actual early receiving task for the tour. Song and Yue remained for a few more minutes without making them a promise of future hours. Yue said she would miss her. Song answered that she would miss Yue too and still wanted the southern road. The sentence held both truths without balancing one away. Yue was glad she could hear it without beginning another argument.

shoal_e18_close_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_close_08.text: On Day Three Hundred Seventy-Four, the carrier received the actual tour case and the musician's separate property before the ordinary departure. Song's booked seat, shared road lodging, and meals belonged to her accepted tour arrangement paid from its own source and earned income. No mine escort funds were used. The road would take its actual time. Her sister would not receive a visit before the performer had physically reached the relevant stop.

shoal_e18_close_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_close_09.text: Yue stood at the permitted departure edge with the other people saying goodbye. Song gave no secret instruction to follow. She asked Yue to write if she wanted, using the offered ordinary receiving address on her tour list. A letter would need a real route and cost. Yue accepted the narrow invitation. It was more valuable because it did not pretend the road between them had vanished.

shoal_e18_close_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_close_10.text: The coach left at its ordinary hour. Its wheels caught a rough patch, and the passengers shifted rather than floating serenely away. Song waved once from the window and then turned to the musician, probably to discuss the piece he was hoping she would leave alone. Yue watched until the coach passed the last visible bend. Departure had the plain physical effect of making a familiar person absent from the lane.

shoal_e18_close_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_close_11.text: She returned to a town still busy with its own meals and work. At the rehearsal room, the keeper removed Song's current notice and posted the next performer's actual hours. The change looked abrupt. It was also the venue's ordinary livelihood. The room had not become disloyal by making space for another accepted artist after Song's booked use ended. Yue knew that and still paused before walking past it.

shoal_e18_close_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_close_12.text: At Bo's shop, Jin was negotiating a net repair while Bo advised a customer on a fastening from his seated place. They had completed the finite care account and still had ordinary limits and costs. Their next livelihood was narrower, uncertain, and theirs. Bo asked Yue whether Song had gone. She said yes. He nodded and offered her a stool that did not pretend she had nowhere else she might choose to be.

shoal_e18_close_13.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_close_13.text: The apprentice arrived for his actual accepted paid interval. Yue left before their work began, not wishing to turn a shop's productive hours into an audience for her farewell mood. She walked the quieter lane and heard the tide bell clearly because no cart was passing. Song might have noticed a phrase in it. Yue simply listened until it ended. Absence did not need to make every sound into a message from the departed.

shoal_e18_close_14.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_close_14.text: On Day Three Hundred Seventy-Five, Han posted a new ordinary corrective-work offer under the Six-Reach Signal Case Review source. It concerned current freight-signal housings whose mechanical covers and receiving instructions had produced separate actual questions. One owner wanted a missing hinge measured; another wanted a closing sequence checked after ordinary repair. The source would compare offered devices within a named scope, leaving fire-damaged private property and household compensation with their own current processes.

shoal_e18_close_15.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_close_15.text: The new appropriation held one hundred sixty copper. Eighty funded twenty four-hour receiving shifts at four each; forty-eight funded four qualified twelve-copper bench assessments; twenty current materials; twelve permitted messages. Its accepted work window would run from Day Three Hundred Seventy-Seven through Four Hundred Two, closing the next day. It had no claim on the finished restoration, care, or earlier receiving accounts.

shoal_e18_close_16.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_close_16.text: Yue read the ordinary work role and its hours. She would receive sources, owners' permissions, and actual assessment findings. Qualified people would perform the mechanical checks under their own scopes. Nothing asked her to power a new housing or lift a heavy assembly. The wage was smaller than her prior five-copper shift and the task narrower. She could refuse it or accept its actual conditions without treating either answer as a judgment on her cultivation.

shoal_e18_close_17.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_close_17.text: Han said the offer had other applicants and would not remain reserved forever. Yue asked for the accepted reply deadline and took the permitted copy home to read. She had completed her old labor term; accepting this would create a new one. The institution needed a named ordinary receiver because corrected work otherwise tended to dissolve into somebody's assumed spare hours. The proposed fund made those hours concrete enough to examine.

shoal_e18_close_18.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_close_18.text: At the inn she compared the new dates with current room costs and any later road. The work could support the remaining port stay from actual earned wages, but those wages would arrive only after performed shifts. Her present own savings and settled earnings covered the interval beforehand. She named no incoming tour payment because Song's art was Song's. She named no care surplus because the finite deposit had been used under its actual plan.

shoal_e18_close_19.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_close_19.text: The little offer sheet lay beside her private practice notebook. The two asked different questions. One described work she could do with ordinary attention and paid hours. The other recorded a small application that would need its own actual qualification before any change. More money did not open another pair of routes. More opened routes did not make the office's mechanical assessments hers. She could respect both crafts and still need supper.

shoal_e18_close_20.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_close_20.text: Outside, someone practiced the ordinary refrain Yue had heard during Song's earlier performance. Yue could remember the song whether or not she had taken the offered beginner lesson. Hearing it was not evidence that she could sing it well. She let the performer outside own his actual voice. The new work offer waited for a decision she would make after sleeping rather than while wishing the departing coach could be called back.

shoal_e18_close_21.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_close_21.text: In the morning, Yue folded the offer carefully and went to the clerk at the named reply time. She had no accepted outgoing mine role yet and no wish to remain indefinitely. Twenty actual receiving shifts could fit before a later road if she chose their terms. The next conversation would concern present owners, mechanical limits, and wages. It would begin with a real yes or no, after Song's real departure.

shoal_e18_close_22.speaker: narrator
shoal_e18_close_22.text: Han greeted her without assuming an answer and cleared a place for the paper. Yue asked which owner would receive the assessments and how an unresolved result would be reported. The clerk brought the terms instead of promising that the work would end in success. She read them in the light, with time to notice what the job asked.
